items.stem: A teammate adds an API key directly into the Dockerfile so the container 'just works'. Why is this wrong?

options.text: The secret is baked into the image and leaks to anyone who pulls it
options.rationale: Correct: secrets in an image are exposed to everyone with image access.
They can; the problem is that a secret must not be one of them.

options.text: It makes the image slightly larger
options.rationale: Size is not the issue; secret exposure is.

options.text: Azure will reject any image with text in it
options.rationale: Azure does not reject the image; the practice is simply insecure.

items.explanation: Correct: secrets in an image are exposed to everyone with image access.

items.stem: Which TWO properties make a cloud deployment process trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is repeatable rather than a one-off manual click-through
options.rationale: Correct: repeatability makes deployments predictable and auditable.

options.text: Promotion to production passes a review gate
options.rationale: Correct: review before production catches issues early.

options.text: It is done quickly outside business hours with no record
options.rationale: Speed without a record undermines auditability.

options.text: It skips staging to reach production faster
options.rationale: Skipping staging removes a key validation step.

items.explanation: Correct: repeatability makes deployments predictable and auditable.

items.stem: A new release is failing in production. What capability lets you recover fastest and safely?

options.text: A tested rollback to the previous known-good image
options.rationale: Correct: a rollback restores service while the failure is investigated.

options.text: Editing files directly on the production server
options.rationale: Hand-editing production is unrepeatable and risky.

options.text: Waiting to see if the errors stop on their own
options.rationale: Hoping is not a recovery strategy.

options.text: Deleting the logs to clear the alerts
options.rationale: Removing logs hides the problem rather than fixing it.

items.explanation: Correct: a rollback restores service while the failure is investigated.
